audit.why: Both chart layers already match the packet chart and each other: L1 skill, L2-L3 Illaoi, Levels 4-5 and Level 6 skill, first item and 2+ items Illaoi. That fits a 50.90% win rate over 1000 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Levels 4-5 spike was attributed to 'his early ult' in two places. He has no ultimate before level 6.
audit.why: Grim Deliverance (R) is 110/95/80s and only exists from 6. What actually punishes you at 4-5 is his W: it stabs out to 850 and pulls you toward him on a 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s cooldown — the exact tool that drags you off your tentacle field, which is what wants.foe[0] already describes without naming it.
audit.corrected: whys[3], spikes[1] and early rewritten around the W pull with its range and cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] had 3 entries where 4 are expected — the late-game spike was absent, a structural gap.
audit.why: His passive, Determination, fills from attacks and abilities against champions and lets him revive. That is the defining late-game fact of this matchup and appears nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] created with before:null — the revive, and what it means for committing a 120s ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one of Zaahen's abilities was named anywhere on the page — every reference was the literal word 'Ultimate' or 'his key ability', including focus.text and the cooldown breakdown.
audit.why: The kit gives real behaviour to work with: The Darkin Glaive (Q) is an auto-attack reset that heals him and knocks you up on the recast, 10/9/8/7/6s; Aureate Rush (E) is a dash on 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s that deals percent-health damage, so armour alone misreads the trade; Grim Deliverance (R) heals for a portion of the damage it deals, 110s at rank 1 against your 120s.
audit.corrected: Names, numbers and the reset tell written into focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, mid and late. That also clears the packet's second defect — the page had zero cooldown-sequencing cues.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization prescribed no anti-heal at all.
audit.why: _missing carries needs-antiheal: both The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance heal him, and the passive revive compounds it. This is the opposite of the yasuo and yone pages, where anti-heal was prescribed against champions with no healing.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling added to report[8] and Grievous Wounds to late.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even out: his early ult punishes you whenever you fight off your tentacles — stay planted.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out: his W pulls you 850 units off your tentacles — never fight past the field's edge.

edits.before: Level 6 is even — his ult trades against your Leap of Faith commit, and whoever commits second wins.
edits.after: Level 6 is even — Grim Deliverance is 110s, Leap of Faith 120s; whoever commits second wins.

edits.before: His early ult window — only fight while standing on your tentacles.
edits.after: His 850-range W pull — only fight while standing on your tentacles.

Determination fills from every hit he lands on you and lets him revive once full, so a late fight that looks even is one you have to win twice. Grievous Wounds and a tentacle field planted beside terrain are what make the second kill possible.

edits.before: From level 2 you are the bully — Harsh Lesson slams with tentacle follow-up out-trade him, and by 3 the field plus Test of Spirit zones him off the wave entirely. One caveat arrives at 4-5: his ult shows up early and punishes any fight you take away from your tentacles, so bully strictly from your setup and never chase past its edge.
edits.after: From level 2 you are the bully — Harsh Lesson slams with tentacle follow-up out-trade him, and by 3 the field plus Test of Spirit zones him off the wave. The caveat at 4-5 is his W: it stabs out 850 and pulls you toward him, off your tentacles, on a 14s cooldown. Bully from your setup and never chase past its edge.

edits.before: Level 6 is a commit-chicken standoff — his ult against your Leap of Faith, and whoever burns first usually loses — but first item resolves it your way: tentacle DPS plus sustain out-brawls him in every extended trade. Force long fights on planted ground, land the spirit test to double your damage sources, and watch his health bar lose the argument.
edits.after: Level 6 is a commit-chicken standoff — Grim Deliverance (R) is 110s at rank 1 against your 120s Leap of Faith, so whoever burns first usually loses. First item resolves it your way. Watch The Darkin Glaive (Q): it is an auto-attack reset that heals him and the recast knocks you up, so the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast.

edits.before: Two-plus items is the punchline: his kit wants extended fights, and extended fights are exactly what Illaoi wins. Side-lane on terraformed ground, ult his engage the moment he commits, and out-brawl him with the storm swinging. His only outs are short trades and disengage — deny both by holding W to stick and E to punish the retreat.
edits.after: Two-plus items is the punchline: his kit wants extended fights, and extended fights are what Illaoi wins. Buy Grievous Wounds first though — The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance both heal him, and his passive revives him once it fills. Side-lane on terraformed ground, hold W to stick, and E to punish the retreat.

notes: This page named none of Zaahen's abilities — every reference was the bare word 'Ultimate', including focus.text and the loading screen. It also claimed his ultimate punishes you at levels 4-5, which is impossible before 6; the real level 4-5 threat is his 850-range W pull that drags you off your tentacles.
